answer.label: Not Francis of Assisi — the Serenity Prayer
answer.sourceLine: Not Francis of Assisi. This is the familiar Serenity Prayer, generally credited to Reinhold Niebuhr; Winnifred Wygal's early records are central to its history, and the wording evolved.

source.excerpt: God grant me the serenity … and the wisdom to know the difference.
trail: Quote Investigator ↗ traces Wygal's diary and publications and favors Niebuhr's authorship.

source.rightsNote: This is a twentieth-century prayer in an evolving wording. Without an identified first publication of the exact form, no public-domain clearance is asserted.

author.name: Reinhold Niebuhr
author.heading: About Reinhold Niebuhr
author.bio: Reinhold Niebuhr was an American Protestant theologian. The Serenity Prayer is closely associated with him, although its circulation and wording also owe much to Winnifred Wygal.

cite.sourceCitation: Serenity Prayer, generally credited to Reinhold Niebuhr. Early records and variants traced in Quote Investigator, “Serenity Prayer,” December 24, 2019. Exact first publication of displayed wording unconfirmed.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: Francis's name is not supported: the documented trail ↗ concerns a modern prayer associated with Niebuhr and Wygal.

items.why: Francis's name is not supported: the documented trail ↗ concerns a modern prayer associated with Niebuhr and Wygal.

misattribution.truthLine: Not Francis of Assisi. This is the familiar Serenity Prayer, generally credited to Reinhold Niebuhr; Winnifred Wygal's early records are central to its history, and the wording evolved.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The prayer reached readers through changing versions, rather than one fixed formula. Quote Investigator ↗ documents Wygal's early records and her credit to Niebuhr, which is a modern transmission history rather than evidence of a medieval Francis text.
